catch_records.vessel: Sea Watch on their full-day trip
catch_records.source_excerpt: The Sea Watch on their full-day trip returned with 1 Wahoo, 150 Yellowfin Tuna, 58 Dorado, 2 Skipjack Tuna and 1 Yellowtail. Passports are not currently required for these trips. Current sniper-style jigs have been getting bit well, but it’s also a good idea to bring a 20–30 lb live-bait setup.

catch_records.vessel: San Diego full day offshore trip
catch_records.source_excerpt: The San Diego full day offshore trip finished up their trip with 175 Yellowfin Tuna and 12 Dorado. Fly-lined live bait on 15–30 lb tackle has been getting it done, along with smaller-sized sniper-style jigs. Be sure to bring multiple hook sizes, ranging from #2 to 2/0. Passports are not required.

field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: The rock fishing was great for blues and blacks near Ano Nuevo. The halibut are still biting up the coast from 4 Mile to Davenport. There was a nice 45 pound sea bass caught trolling a hoochies and sardine near 4 Mile. The anglers near Capitola caught a mix of rock fish and halibut. I did not hear of any tuna today. The wind was down in the morning due to the fog but it did blow at 11:30. The swell was 4 feet but has dropped.

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast September 17, 2026 Big Albacore Highlight Eureka’s Weekend Tuna Run Gabe Gibbs of Montana made his first trip on the ocean a success by landing his first-ever Albacore. Gibbs is a current CR student and baseball player who was fishing on Steller Sunrise with Capt. Lowell Wallace Sunday. Photo courtesy of John Lanz It was a Saturday that Eureka tuna anglers won’t soon forget. After several less-than-stellar days, the stars finally aligned for the small fleet that made the 30- to 35-mile run south. It wasn’t the number of fish that stood out — it was the size. The majority of the albacore caught were 25 pounds or better, with some fish pushing 40 pounds. The fish were reportedly spread out along the 125-line, from the 46-line down to the 38-line, where a hard break pushed water temperatures up six degrees. The action ranged from boats reporting single hookups to others hooking eight at a time, and everything in between. A couple of common themes emerged from the fleet: when the fish are this big, you only have room for so many, and several anglers left fish biting at the end of the day. field_reports.name: Dockside Depoe Bay Daily Report
field_reports.summary: Effective Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 12:01 a.m. through September 26, 2026, at 11:59 p.m., for the ocean recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, retention of coho salmon is allowed, with a daily bag limit of two salmon (no fin clip requirement). Beginning Sunday, September 27, 2026, the season remains open through October 31, 2026, all salmon, except coho salmon, with a daily bag limit of two salmon. The minimum size for kept Chinook salmon is 24 inches in total length.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: The same crew went right back where they left them. There were tons of smaller (8-10) tuna but only one jumbo. The crew ended up with 43. Tomorrow is our last charter of the year and then we are sitting out the big wind for a few days before we head out for a few crew trips. ​Mike C 9/22. It got better. WFO. Foamers.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: Tomorrow's in-season call with NMFS and the State of Oregon, to discuss Oregon's (SOF) recreational ocean salmon fisheries is cancelled. For the 2026 recreational non-mark selective coho fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, the estimated catch through September 20, 2026, is approximately 22,250 coho salmon, or 87% of the 25,700 quota. The expected coho salmon catch for Saturday September 26, 2026, which was previously adopted and remains open as scheduled, does not provide sufficient balance to add any additional days to the fishery. PREVIOUS ACTION TAKEN: • Effective Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 12:01 a.m. through September 26, 2026, at 11:59 p.m., for the ocean recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, retention of coho salmon is allowed, with a daily bag limit of two salmon (no fin clip requirement). Beginning Sunday, September 27, 2026, the season remains open through October 31, 2026, all salmon, except coho salmon, with a daily bag limit of two salmon. The minimum size for kept Chinook salmon is 24 inches in total length.
